title: Tighter Variable-Set Bound for the LowMC Interpolation Attack
summary: The analysis bounds the transformed-variable set by the original set and approximates the parameter e by the size of W; a tighter bound is needed to sharpen attack complexity.

formal_statement.body: For the optimized interpolation attack on LowMC, derive a tighter general upper bound for the size of the transformed-variable set $U^{\prime\prime}$ than the currently used bound $|U^{\prime\prime}| \leq |U|$, and use that bound to sharpen the attack's data, time, and memory complexity. The existing analysis lacks a good bound for $|U^{\prime\prime}|$, replaces it by $|U|$, and assumes $e \approx |W|$; the refined bound should therefore state the necessary conditions on $U^{\prime\prime}$, $e$, $W$, and the other attack parameters under which the resulting complexity expressions improve.

scope.domain: Algebraic cryptanalysis and resource analysis of the optimized interpolation attack on LowMC.
assumptions: The existing analysis assumes that e is approximately the cardinality of W.
parameters: U'': the transformed-variable set whose size is to be bounded
U: the original variable set furnishing the current upper bound
e and W: attack quantities related by the existing approximation and used in the complexity expressions
scope.unresolved_remainder: Derive a tighter general upper bound for the size of U'' and state the parameter conditions under which it improves the attack's data, time, and memory complexity.

progress.summary: The source reports that no good general bound for the transformed-variable set is available, so its size is replaced by that of U and e is approximated by the size of W. Refining the bound and the resulting complexity analysis remains unresolved.
citation_labels: Itai Dinur et al., Optimized Interpolation Attacks on LowMC
